IM10-01.why: Four bare integers of similar size; 30 is arguably the product-shaped distractor but I cannot show it illegal without factoring, so nothing is eliminated.

IM10-02.why: 108 is exactly 2x54, the classic un-halved double-count intermediate, so it and its half cannot both be legal and the halved member is the answer shape for a diagonal count.

IM10-03.why: 650000 is the odd one out by form - the only non-power-of-ten, and it reads as an additive (2.5+4) trap - but the three remaining powers of ten are mutually indistinguishable without multiplying.

IM10-04.why: Every option is one of the table's own category labels, so the option set adds no constraint beyond the table.

IM10-05.why: 35 restates the stem's given percent as a degree measure (an option encoding its own given, wrong unit), but 126/105/63 are all legal degree measures under 360.

IM10-06.why: 108 is literally 9x12, the area left in the given unit, and 36 is that divided by 3 only once, so both are step-short values in a two-step conversion; 12 also merely restates a given dimension.

IM10-07.why: 2200, 2420, 2662 form a x1.1 chain from the given 2000, so the set encodes years 1, 2 and 3; the stem names 2 years, which is the second link, and 2200 is visibly the one-year intermediate.

IM10-08.why: 471 = 314 + 157 and 785 = 471 + 314, so the set contains component areas and their partial sums; 314 is a single bare component and a total surface area must be the sum of two parts.

IM10-09.why: 2 is the sum of P's coordinates untransformed, an option that answers the question before any of the stem's operations; 12/-12 are a sign pair far outside the scale set by a shift of 4 on coordinates of size 3 and 5.

IM10-10.why: A fully symmetric sign-and-reciprocal quartet (2, -2, 0.5, -0.5); no member is distinguishable from the set alone.

IM10-11.why: Four small integers with no dominance, unit or form asymmetry among them.

IM10-12.why: 1130.4 is exactly 3x376.8, the cylinder value with the 1/3 dropped, and the stem hands you the 1/3 explicitly, so the un-thirded member is illegal.

IM10-13.why: 16 is 5+11, the two stem constants added, an option assembled from the givens; the remaining three cannot be separated without solving.

IM10-14.why: 15 restates the stem's own constant, so it is the give-back option; 28/14/11 are indistinguishable from the set alone.

IM10-15.why: 150 is the bare unit value (population divided by the ratio's denominator) and 450 is exactly 3x150 matching the ratio's numerator, so 150 is a one-step-short intermediate sitting in the set beside its own completion.

IM10-16.why: Four weekday names; no ordering, magnitude or form relation exists among them.

IM10-17.why: 21 restates a stem value; 24 and 15 are the after- and before-ranges and 24-15 = 9 is also in the set, so with the stem asking for the INCREASE the two raw ranges are components, not the answer.

IM10-18.why: 2 is an order of magnitude too small to be the range of scores spanning three stems; 21, 15 and 9 are all legal spreads.

IM10-19.why: All four are legal angle measures under 180 with no dominance or form asymmetry.

IM10-20.why: 1/11 inverts the numerator of 11/24 (the reciprocal-of-the-sum trap) and cannot coexist with it; 1/24 is the unit fraction on the same denominator, i.e. the product rather than the sum the stem names.

IM10-21.why: 26 = 2x13 and 16 = 2x8 are simple doublings of the two given coordinates; a distance between two points must combine both givens, not double one.

IM10-22.why: 2/5 is the OTHER named sector (144/360), answering a different question than the stem asks, and 1/3 corresponds to no named angle; 7/40 is half of 7/20, a denominator that cannot arise from a 360-degree whole.

IM10-23.why: 8 restates the stem's stated median; 10 is the average of the other two options 8 and 12, and a median of an even-sized set is exactly an average of two middle values.

IM10-24.why: 121 restates the given area and 11 is the bare side length; 11, 22, 44 form a doubling chain and a perimeter is four sides, so the top of the chain is the only completed value.

IM10-25.why: 16 is the odd one out by magnitude against the tight 34/36/38 cluster, but those three are mutually indistinguishable without solving.

IM10-26.why: 17 and 18 read as the largest root / the bound itself rather than a count of squares in the interval, while 11 and 12 are the genuine off-by-one count pair.

IM10-27.why: Three options (450, 530, 730) are year-to-year increases present in the stem's table and 820 is not one at all; the stem asks for the GREATEST, so 450 and 530 are dominated by 730, which also sits in the set.

IM10-28.why: 120 cannot be the LEAST qualifying value when 108, also a multiple of 12, is available in the same set - dominance kills it outright.

IM10-29.why: 25 restates the given number of minutes in the wrong unit and 12.5 is simply half of that given; an answer in degrees should not be the elapsed-minute count or a halving of it.

IM10-30.why: 18 = 25-7 is the two givens subtracted and 12.5 is half of a given, both assembled straight from the stem's numbers rather than from a leg relation.
